Lo stadio FIGO IVA è definito dall'invas:
FIGO stage IVA is defined by invasion of the bladder or rectal mucosa, proven by biopsy. On MRI the signs are: loss of the hypointense line of the muscular wall on T2, nodular tissue protruding into the lumen, focal wall thickening in continuity with the tumor. Bullous edema of the mucosa alone is not enough.
Pitfall of this exam: on coronal T2 the mass appears surrounded by fluid as if it were inside the bladder, but the surrounding fluid is partly the gel distending the vagina and the tumor crater. On the sagittal and axial images the posterior bladder wall remains a thin, continuous dark line: infiltration is not demonstrated. Any suspicion of invasion must always be checked on at least two planes.
In the registry this patient is stage IVA: the infiltrated organ is not specified, and mucosal invasion is confirmed by endoscopy, not by MRI. MRI serves mainly to exclude it when the wall is intact, and to guide radiotherapy.
In such a bulky tumor the treatment is chemoradiotherapy in any case; the risk of vesicovaginal or rectovaginal fistula during treatment should be mentioned. Complete with distant staging (para-aortic lymph nodes, lungs).

FIGO stage IVA is defined by invasion of the bladder or rectal mucosa, proven by biopsy. On sagittal and axial images the posterior bladder wall remains a thin continuous dark line: infiltration is not demonstrated. Any suspicion of invasion must always be checked on at least two planes.
In the registry this patient is stage IVA: the infiltrated organ is not specified, and mucosal invasion is confirmed by endoscopy, not by MRI. MRI serves mainly to exclude it when the wall is intact, and to guide radiotherapy.
